SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Profuse watery diarrhea for 3 days, occurring roughly hourly while awake.  
  • Associated crampy, central lower-abdominal pain (intermittent, ~6/10).  
  • Nausea and occasional vomiting, particularly after milk ingestion.  
  • Subjective fever (“burning up”) but no recorded temperature.  
  • No hematochezia or melena.  
  • Slightly reduced urinary frequency but still passing urine.
- Possible contact: Brother has had similar illness for 5 days, now improving.
- Past medical history: Denies chronic illnesses; otherwise fit and well.
- Medications: Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented) for fever/pain; no regular prescriptions.
- Social history:  
  • Lives with mother and sister.  
  • Employment: Government office, Central London.  
  • Smoking: Social/occasional (mainly on Fridays).  
  • Alcohol: 1 beer on some weekdays; binge drinking 1–2×/month; advised reduction.  
- Family history: Father with stage III colon cancer.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies (NKDA).

Objective:
- No in-person examination performed (video consult).  
- No vitals available.  
- No investigations performed to date.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute watery diarrhea with abdominal cramps  
   - Assessment: Likely infectious gastroenteritis.  
   - Differential diagnosis: Lactose intolerance flare, viral gastroenteritis (e.g., norovirus), food-borne bacterial infection.  
   - Investigations planned: None immediately; consider stool culture and basic bloods if no improvement within 48 h or signs of dehydration.  
   - Treatment:  
     • Oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte) – OTC.  
     • Clear fluids + progressive soft diet (soups, mashed foods) as tolerated.  
     • Paracetamol as needed for fever/pain.  
     • Avoid alcohol.  
   - Safety-net: Return/telephone review if symptoms persist >48 h, worsen, develop blood in stool, unable to keep fluids down, or signs of dehydration (e.g., no urine, dizziness).  

2. Risk of dehydration  
   - Assessment: Mild risk given hourly watery stools and subjective fever.  
   - Treatment: Emphasize adequate oral rehydration; monitor urine output.  
   - Escalation: If oral intake inadequate or clinical deterioration, advise urgent assessment for IV fluids.

Quality checks:

• Missing/expected elements: Objective examination findings and vitals; detailed medication reconciliation (OTC, supplements); drug doses; immunization status.  
• Internal conflicts: None identified.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; minimal background noise; no significant inaudible sections.
